newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS -- Prices flat, bias firmer.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS -- Prices flat, bias firmer.

text.p: U.S. municipal bond prices were flat to a hint firmer early Tuesday amid a busy new issue slate set to include two Virginia Housing Development Authority deals totaling $325.7 million at 1100 EDT.
"(Prices are) unchanged, maybe a tad firmer from where they went out last night," a trader said.
A second trader said Tuesday morning's muni cash levels were difficult to quantify because when muni futures swooned on Monday, "the bidside just disappeared."
"So I'm just guesstimating what the bid would have been yesterday at the close versus now, and it's probably up about a basis point," he said.

In competition action, Virginia HDA is expected to price two deals -- $225 million and $100.7 million -- at 1100 EDT. A trader added that when high-grade issues come competitively, they generally come aggressively priced.
"So there'll be no steals in that marketplace," he said.
In negotiated action, Smith Barney Inc tentatively priced $206 million Broward County, Fla., school certificates of participation at a top yield of 5.53 percent in 2017.
PaineWebber Inc tentatively priced $98 million Virginia Port Authority revenue bonds at a top yield of 5.731 percent in 2027.
Wednesday's negotiated action is expected to include a $540 million Puerto Rico Public Buildings Authority deal.
"It will appeal to people who are looking for the specialty states that are not around," a trader said.

In the government market, the benchmark 30-year bond was up 6/32 at 97-21/32 to yield 6.81 percent. In debt futures, the September municipal contract was up 4/32 at 116-19/32. The September T-bond contract was up 9/32 at 110-28/32. The MOB spread was 183 ticks.
